title: Resonance
concept:
Filters have a second control called Resonance (sometimes labelled Q). It boosts the frequencies right at the cutoff point, creating a peak in the frequency response.

At low resonance the filter is gentle and smooth — it just rolls off the high frequencies softly. As you increase resonance, a narrow band of frequencies around the cutoff starts to ring. The sound takes on a nasal, vocal-like quality. Think of the 'wah' pedal sound on a guitar — that is a resonant filter in action.

At very high resonance values the filter begins to self-oscillate: it produces its own tone even without any input signal. This is a characteristic sound of classic synthesizers and is used deliberately in many styles of electronic music.

The filter is already set to a mid cutoff so the effect of resonance is clearly audible. Raise the Resonance to 15 to hear the peak emerge.

task.instruction: Raise the Filter's Resonance to 15. Adjust the Resonance knob on the Filter component and listen to the ringing peak appear at the cutoff frequency.
